stories.headline: WikiTrace links agent memory back to evidence

source.title: WikiTrace: Learning Evidence-Linked Memory for Long-Horizon Agents
source.scope: Reviewed the complete paper abstract, method, five benchmark evaluations, same-insights baseline and documented memory-induced degradation limits.
source.freshness_reason: Individually justified 168-hour fallback: the November 10 original paper supplies unique benchmark and ablation evidence not found in newer reviewed technical candidates.

read_evidence.scope: Reviewed the complete paper abstract, method, five benchmark evaluations, same-insights baseline and documented memory-induced degradation limits.

stories.summary: WikiTrace introduces an evidence-linked memory system for long-running language-model agents. Instead of storing conclusions alone, it preserves insights, rationales and trajectories, then retrieves them across five agent benchmarks. The authors report gains over prior memory methods and over a same-insights baseline, while identifying and reducing memory-induced performance degradation.
stories.why_it_matters: When testing agent memory, retain the source evidence and reasoning path beside each stored insight. Compare against both no-memory and same-insight baselines, then log cases where retrieved memories degrade decisions instead of assuming every retained trace helps.
stories.related_coverage: Broader technical discovery; complete original paper and stated limitations reviewed.
stories.image_alt_intent: An agent follows a long task path while memory cards remain visibly linked to source evidence, rationale and prior trajectory checkpoints.

stories.headline: A trust pyramid turns generated code into evidence

source.title: All Code Is Slop (Except Mine)
source.scope: Reviewed the complete original talk article covering the trust pyramid, architecture, type systems, linting, tests, runtime verification and limits of aesthetic judgments.
source.freshness_reason: Within the authorized 168-hour window; selected for a concrete verification framework after the exact companion video failed protected playback.

read_evidence.scope: Reviewed the complete original talk article covering the trust pyramid, architecture, type systems, linting, tests, runtime verification and limits of aesthetic judgments.

stories.summary: Lauren Tan argues that generated code should earn trust through layered evidence rather than style or authorship. Her trust pyramid moves from architecture and type constraints through linting and tests to runtime verification. The framework separates aesthetic objections from observable failures, giving teams a repeatable way to review both human and machine-written changes.
stories.why_it_matters: Define required evidence before accepting generated code: architectural boundaries, type checks, lint rules, tests and runtime observations. Record which layer caught each defect, and treat persuasive formatting or familiar style as weak signals unless supported by executable verification.
stories.related_coverage: Top 10 topic 3; original article fully reviewed, while its YouTube companion failed protected signed-out playback.
stories.image_alt_intent: A code change ascends a five-level trust pyramid labeled architecture, types, lint, tests and runtime evidence, with failures caught at each layer.

stories.summary: Reuters found procurement records showing a PLA-linked Chinese university bought two Nvidia H200 chips for 874,700 yuan and separately rented H200 access despite United States restrictions. stories.headline: Agent pilots start with workflow evidence, not ambition

source.title: From AI ambition to business impact
source.scope: Reviewed the complete Microsoft article, workflow-redesign argument, named customer cases, vendor-reported claims and the distinction between adoption activity and measured business outcomes.
source.freshness_reason: Within the authorized 72-hour window at research start; selected for a noncoding workflow redesign procedure while preserving vendor-claim attribution.

read_evidence.scope: Reviewed the complete Microsoft article, workflow-redesign argument, named customer cases, vendor-reported claims and the distinction between adoption activity and measured business outcomes.

stories.summary: Microsoft argues that organizations get more value by redesigning complete workflows than by adding isolated AI features. Its customer examples are vendor-reported, so they should guide questions rather than prove outcomes. The practical lesson is to define the baseline, decision rights and measurable result before an agent is introduced into everyday work.
stories.why_it_matters: Pick one noncoding workflow, record its current time and error baseline, map every handoff, and define the agent’s allowed actions. Run a bounded trial with human approval, then compare results and document which vendor claims remain unverified.
stories.related_coverage: Broader agent discovery; complete vendor article reviewed with customer-result claims kept attributed.

stories.headline: Recursive self-improvement depends on inspectable assumptions

source.title: Recursive Self-Improvement
source.scope: Reviewed the complete essay and transcript across software research loops, bottleneck assumptions, compute constraints, evaluation, feedback quality and explicit uncertainty.
source.freshness_reason: Within the authorized 72-hour window at research start; selected from Top 10 topic 2 for a rigorous noncoding decision framework rather than a prediction claim.

read_evidence.scope: Reviewed the complete essay and transcript across software research loops, bottleneck assumptions, compute constraints, evaluation, feedback quality and explicit uncertainty.

stories.summary: Dwarkesh Patel examines recursive self-improvement as a chain of assumptions about research automation, feedback quality, compute and the ability to improve the systems doing the research. The essay does not establish a timetable. Its value is a structured map of bottlenecks and uncertainty that decision-makers can test instead of treating “self-improvement” as one event.
stories.why_it_matters: When evaluating recursive-improvement claims, list each required step and the evidence supporting it. Mark unknown feedback, compute and evaluation constraints separately, then define what new observation would change your decision rather than debating one all-or-nothing forecast.
stories.related_coverage: Top 10 topic 2; complete original essay and transcript reviewed.
stories.image_alt_intent: A decision map breaks recursive AI improvement into separate loops for research, feedback, compute and evaluation, with uncertain assumptions visibly flagged.

audience_fit.intended_user: Leaders and general readers evaluating strategic claims about recursive AI improvement without needing technical implementation skills.
audience_fit.practical_action: Break one forecast into required steps, label its evidence and mark the feedback, compute and evaluation assumptions.
audience_fit.review_action: A decision owner checks which observation would confirm, weaken or overturn each assumption before changing plans.
audience_fit.usable_outcome: An inspectable assumption map replaces a single all-or-nothing prediction with bounded evidence and decision triggers.
